title: Pyramid of numbers sheet
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Ecosystems (7D); atoms, elements and molecules (7H)
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 56 (Pyramid of numbers sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 56: Pyramids of numbers and bioaccumulation. To understand how pyramids of numbers show feeding relationships and how toxins build up along a food chain

questions.q: A pond has 1 heron, 50 fish, 2,000 water fleas and lots of algae. Which level is widest?
questions.model: Pyramids put producers at the base. There are far more algae than anything else, so the bottom bar is the widest.

questions.q: Why is an oak-caterpillar pyramid not a true pyramid?
questions.a: One big oak feeds many caterpillars, so the base is narrow
A toxin building up higher in a food chain

questions.q: Draw pyramids of numbers for two food chains on the sheet and explain why one is an odd shape.
questions.a: Correct bars; oak chain explained by one large producer
questions.model: Teacher draws the grass → rabbit → fox pyramid with a wide base bar.

questions.q: A mouse eats 10 seeds each with 1 unit of pesticide; an owl eats 20 mice. How many units in the owl?
Why might banning a pesticide take years to help birds of prey recover?
questions.a: Toxins stay in the environment and bodies; breeding numbers take time to rise

questions.q: Big question: how is the pesticide linked to dying birds of prey?
questions.a: It passes up the food chain and builds up in the top predators.
